title: Albigensian Crusade 1213: How a Heresy Shaped Southern France
hook: A secret religious war erupts in 1213, redrawing Languedoc's borders and shocking medieval Europe forever.
description:
A secret religious war erupts in 1213, redrawing Languedoc's borders and shocking medieval Europe forever, as maps reveal the Albigensian Crusade's brutal legacy.

beats.say: In 1209 the French crown and Pope Innocent III unite, marking the first map where Languedoc splinters under crusader banners.
By 1210 crusader forces under Simon de Montfort seize the fortified town of Béziers, its walls crumble and the map flashes red.
In 1211 the decisive siege of Carcassonne forces the city to capitulate, turning its citadel into a crusader stronghold.
The 1212 Council of Toulouse formalizes the Inquisition, and the map now shades the newly-administered dioceses in violet.
At the Battle of Muret in 1213 Simon de Montfort crushes the Count of Toulouse, expanding crusader territory eastward.
Later that year the crusaders raze the Cathar refuge at Minerve, its ruins appear as a black scar on the map.
By 1215 the Papal legate imposes the Treaty of Meaux, sealing the French crown's control over most of Languedoc.
In 1229 the Treaty of Paris finally ends the war, but the map now shows isolated pockets of lingering Cathar belief.
Surprisingly, the crusade's brutal tactics sowed the seeds of French centralization, a legacy that reshaped Europe for centuries.
